name: Duty and Taxes - Fuel & Oil
definition: The share of import duties, excise and other non-income taxes levied on fuel and lubricating oil, apportioned to the electricity function, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes customs duty, excise and fuel levies borne on generation fuel; excludes income tax and duties on non-fuel purchases. Enter the duty and tax component only once: if fuel cost is already reported gross of duty, avoid also including that duty here.
synonyms: ["fuel duty","fuel excise","fuel taxes","import duty on fuel"]
alternative_names: {"Duty & Taxes - Fuel":"Duty and Taxes - Fuel & Oil","Fuel Duty and Taxes":"Duty and Taxes - Fuel & Oil","Apportioned Cost: Duty and Taxes - Fuel & Oil":"Duty and Taxes - Fuel & Oil"}

name: Duty and Taxes - Others
definition: The share of duties and non-income taxes on goods and services other than fuel and oil, apportioned to the electricity function, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes import duties on plant, equipment and materials, and other indirect taxes or levies borne on non-fuel purchases; excludes income tax and fuel-related duties, which are reported separately. Recoverable input VAT or GST should be excluded, as it is not a cost to the utility.
synonyms: ["other duties and taxes","import duty on materials","non-fuel taxes","indirect taxes"]
alternative_names: {"Duty & Taxes - Others":"Duty and Taxes - Others","Other Duties and Taxes":"Duty and Taxes - Others","Apportioned Cost: Duty and Taxes - Others":"Duty and Taxes - Others"}

name: Fuel & Oil Expenditure
definition: The share of total fuel and lubricating-oil expenditure apportioned to the electricity function, entered in the utility's local currency. Covers diesel, heavy fuel oil, petrol and lubricants consumed in generation, valued at delivered cost including freight; for multi-utility organisations only the electricity-attributable portion is entered here. Enter fuel cost net of any recoverable duty rebate only where that rebate is not already reported under the duty-and-taxes lines, to avoid double counting.
synonyms: ["fuel and oil cost","apportioned fuel cost","generation fuel expenditure","fuel & lubricants cost"]
alternative_names: {"Apportioned Fuel Cost":"Fuel & Oil Expenditure","Apportioned Cost: Fuel & Oil Expenditure":"Fuel & Oil Expenditure"}

name: Access to Electricity
definition: The share of the population (or households) with access to electricity, expressed as a percentage and stored as a ratio between 0 and 1. It is a national environmental indicator of electrification and unmet demand, not a measure of an individual utility's connection performance. Source it from the census, the national statistics office, or international series such as the World Bank / SE4ALL Tracking framework, for the reporting fiscal year. It is stored as a ratio but displayed as a percentage, and population-based versus household-based definitions can differ materially.
synonyms: ["Electrification rate","Electricity access rate","Access rate"]
alternative_names: {"Electrification Rate":"Access to Electricity","Electricity Access Rate":"Access to Electricity"}

name: Air Connectivity per 1000 People
definition: Air connectivity normalised by population, expressed as a ratio per 1,000 people. It scales the country's air-transport connectivity to the size of its population so that connectivity can be compared across countries of different sizes, describing the logistics environment rather than utility performance. It is derived from the underlying air connectivity figure and the national population from the statistics office. Ensure the connectivity source and population vintage align to the same reporting year.
synonyms: ["Connectivity per 1000 population","Air connectivity per capita","Per-capita air connectivity"]
alternative_names: {"Air Connectivity per 1,000 People":"Air Connectivity per 1000 People","Connectivity per 1000 Population":"Air Connectivity per 1000 People"}

name: Air Connectivity per Unit GDP
definition: Air connectivity normalised by the size of the economy, expressed as a ratio per unit of GDP. It relates the country's air-transport connectivity to its economic output, describing the trade and logistics environment a utility operates within rather than utility performance. It is derived from the underlying air connectivity figure and GDP from the national statistics office or central bank. Keep the connectivity, GDP currency and vintage consistent with the same reporting year.
synonyms: ["Connectivity per unit GDP","Air connectivity to GDP ratio","GDP-adjusted air connectivity"]
alternative_names: {"Air Connectivity to GDP":"Air Connectivity per Unit GDP","Connectivity per GDP":"Air Connectivity per Unit GDP"}

name: Average Household Size
definition: The average number of persons per household, expressed as a ratio of persons per household. It is a demographic context indicator of the operating environment, relevant to per-connection consumption, rather than a utility performance measure. Source it from the census, or derive it as national population divided by number of households, for the reporting fiscal year. Ensure the population and household figures used share the same vintage so the ratio is internally consistent.
synonyms: ["Persons per household","Mean household size","Average family size"]
alternative_names: {"Persons per Household":"Average Household Size","Mean Household Size":"Average Household Size"}

name: Fuel Pricing Regulation
definition: A categorical descriptor of the fuel-pricing regime in the country, selected from a defined option list rather than a numeric value. It captures whether fuel prices are regulated, market-determined or subsidised, describing a policy environment that shapes a utility's generation costs rather than its performance. Record the option that applies for the reporting fiscal year. As a coded category, its option definitions should be applied consistently across countries and years.
synonyms: ["Fuel price regime","Fuel price regulation","Fuel pricing regime"]
alternative_names: {"Fuel Price Regulation":"Fuel Pricing Regulation","Fuel Price Regime":"Fuel Pricing Regulation"}

name: Fuel Supply Access
definition: A categorical descriptor of how the country obtains its fuel supply for power generation, selected from a defined option list rather than a numeric value. It characterises the fuel-logistics environment, such as whether fuel is imported directly, sourced through a distributor, or subject to supply constraints, and is a context attribute rather than a performance measure. Record the option that best reflects the arrangement in place for the reporting fiscal year. Because it is a coded category, ensure the option definitions are applied consistently across utilities.
synonyms: ["Fuel access arrangement","Fuel supply arrangement","Fuel sourcing"]
alternative_names: {"Fuel Access":"Fuel Supply Access","Fuel Supply Arrangement":"Fuel Supply Access"}

name: GDP Per Capita
definition: Gross domestic product divided by total population, expressed in currency, giving average national economic output per person. It characterises the economic operating environment and household ability to pay, not utility performance. Source it from the national statistics office, central bank or IMF figures for the reporting fiscal year. Be explicit about whether the figure is nominal or real, in current or constant prices, and in which currency, as vintage and basis materially affect comparability.
synonyms: ["GDP per head","Income per capita","Per capita GDP"]
alternative_names: {"GDP/capita":"GDP Per Capita","Per Capita GDP":"GDP Per Capita"}

name: Households
definition: The total number of households in the country, expressed as a count. It is a national environmental context figure describing the potential connection base, not the utility's own customer accounts. Source it from the latest census or the national statistics office for the reporting fiscal year. Do not equate national households with the utility's connected customers or metered accounts, which are typically fewer.
synonyms: ["Number of households","Total households","Household count"]
alternative_names: {"Total Households":"Households","Number of Households":"Households"}

name: IATA Air Connectivity Score
definition: The country's air connectivity index score as published by IATA, recorded on an index scale (typically ranging up to around 200) rather than a true percentage despite the stored unit. It is a proxy for the country's remoteness and the ease of moving people, parts and specialists, which shapes a utility's logistics and maintenance costs rather than its performance. Source it from the IATA air connectivity index for the relevant year. Treat it as an index, not a percentage, when interpreting or charting the value.
synonyms: ["Air connectivity index","IATA connectivity score","Connectivity index"]
alternative_names: {"Air Connectivity Index":"IATA Air Connectivity Score","IATA Connectivity Index":"IATA Air Connectivity Score"}

name: Inflation Rate
definition: The annual rate of consumer price inflation, expressed as a percentage. It describes the macroeconomic environment that drives the utility's input costs and the real value of tariffs, rather than utility performance. Source it from the national statistics office consumer price index or the central bank for the reporting fiscal year. Note whether the figure is a period-average or end-of-period rate and the CPI base year used.
synonyms: ["CPI inflation","Consumer price inflation","Price inflation"]
alternative_names: {"CPI Inflation":"Inflation Rate","Consumer Price Inflation":"Inflation Rate"}

name: Islands
definition: The number of islands making up the country, expressed as a count. It characterises the geographic operating environment and the dispersion challenge a utility faces in serving scattered populations, rather than utility performance itself. Source it from the national statistics office or census. Definitions vary between total islands, inhabited islands and islands served by an electricity grid, so use the official census count and note which basis applies.
synonyms: ["Number of islands","Island count","Inhabited islands"]
alternative_names: {"Number of Islands":"Islands","Island Count":"Islands"}

name: Land Area
definition: The total land area of the country, expressed in square kilometres (km2). This describes the physical operating environment a utility works within rather than any aspect of its performance, and is a driver of network reach and geographic dispersion. Source it from the national statistics office or lands department, using the latest official figure for the reporting fiscal year. Record the total national land area, not the utility's service-area footprint, and exclude ocean and exclusive economic zone area.
synonyms: ["Total land area","Country land area","Surface area"]
alternative_names: {"Area (km2)":"Land Area","Total Land Area":"Land Area"}

name: Population
definition: The total resident population of the country, expressed as a count of persons. This is a national environmental context figure describing the market a utility operates within, not the utility's own customer base or served population. Source it from the latest census or the national statistics office mid-year estimate for the reporting fiscal year. Do not confuse national population with the utility's served population or connected customers, which are typically a subset.
synonyms: ["Total population","National population","Resident population"]
alternative_names: {"Total Population":"Population","National Population":"Population"}

name: Rural Population
definition: The share of the national population living in rural areas, expressed as a percentage and stored as a ratio between 0 and 1. It is the complement of the urban share and describes the dispersed-settlement context that raises the cost of extending and maintaining electricity supply. Source it from the census urban/rural classification via the national statistics office. It is stored as a ratio but displayed as a percentage, and the rural definition is country-specific.
synonyms: ["Rural share","Percentage rural","Non-urban population"]
alternative_names: {"% Rural":"Rural Population","Rural Share":"Rural Population"}

name: Unemployment Rate
definition: The share of the labour force that is unemployed and seeking work, expressed as a percentage. It is a macroeconomic environment indicator relevant to household incomes and demand, not a utility performance measure. Source it from the national labour force survey or statistics office for the reporting fiscal year, ideally on the standard ILO definition. Interpret with care in Pacific economies, where large informal and subsistence sectors mean headline rates can understate labour under-utilisation.
synonyms: ["Jobless rate","Labour force unemployment","Unemployment"]
alternative_names: {"Jobless Rate":"Unemployment Rate","Rate of Unemployment":"Unemployment Rate"}

name: Urban Population
definition: The share of the national population living in urban areas, expressed as a percentage and stored as a ratio between 0 and 1. It describes the settlement pattern of the operating environment, which shapes network density and cost to serve, rather than utility performance. Source it from the census urban/rural classification via the national statistics office. Note that it is stored as a ratio but displayed as a percentage, and that the definition of "urban" is country-specific.
synonyms: ["Urban share","Percentage urban","Urbanisation rate"]
alternative_names: {"Urbanisation Rate":"Urban Population","% Urban":"Urban Population"}

name: Accounting Standards
definition: A categorical descriptor of the accounting framework the utility reports its financial statements under, selected from a defined option list, such as IFRS, IPSAS or a local GAAP. It is a utility-level context attribute that affects how financial measures should be compared, rather than a performance measure. Record the framework applied to the reporting fiscal year from the utility's audited financial statements. Apply the option definitions consistently, as differing standards can affect the comparability of reported financial figures.
synonyms: ["Accounting framework","Financial reporting standard","Reporting standard"]
alternative_names: {"Accounting Framework":"Accounting Standards","Financial Reporting Standards":"Accounting Standards"}

name: Electricity Regulation
definition: A categorical descriptor of the electricity-sector regulatory arrangement that applies to the utility, selected from a defined option list, such as an independent regulator, a line ministry or self-regulation. It is a utility-level context attribute framing the oversight environment, not a performance measure. Record the arrangement in place for the reporting fiscal year from the utility's regulatory documentation. Apply the option definitions consistently across utilities and years.
synonyms: ["Regulatory arrangement","Electricity sector regulation","Regulatory regime"]
alternative_names: {"Regulatory Regime":"Electricity Regulation","Electricity Sector Regulation":"Electricity Regulation"}

name: Feeder Type
definition: A categorical descriptor of the predominant feeder type in the utility's distribution network, selected from a defined option list, such as overhead versus underground or urban versus rural feeders. It is a utility-level context attribute describing network configuration, which influences reliability and cost, rather than a performance measure. Record the classification that best represents the network for the reporting fiscal year from the utility's network records. Apply the option definitions consistently so feeder types are comparable across utilities.
synonyms: ["Feeder classification","Distribution feeder type","Feeder configuration"]
alternative_names: {"Feeder Classification":"Feeder Type","Distribution Feeder Type":"Feeder Type"}

name: Power Quality Standards
definition: A categorical descriptor of the power-quality standard or regime the utility operates to, selected from a defined option list. It is a utility-level context attribute describing the technical benchmark for voltage and supply quality, rather than a measure of quality actually delivered. Record the standard in force for the reporting fiscal year from the utility's technical or regulatory documentation. Apply the option definitions consistently so the regime, not the outcome, is being captured.
synonyms: ["Power quality standard","Supply quality standard","Quality of supply standard"]
alternative_names: {"Power Quality Standard":"Power Quality Standards","Quality of Supply Standard":"Power Quality Standards"}

name: Utility Ownership Type
definition: A categorical classification of how the utility is owned, selected from a defined option list, such as state-owned enterprise, government department, private company or public-private partnership. It is a utility-level context attribute that frames how other results should be interpreted, not a performance measure. Record the classification that applies to the reporting entity for the fiscal year from the utility's corporate profile. Apply the option definitions consistently so ownership types are comparable across utilities.
synonyms: ["Ownership type","Ownership structure","Ownership model"]
alternative_names: {"Ownership Type":"Utility Ownership Type","Ownership Structure":"Utility Ownership Type"}

name: Electricity O&M
definition: Direct operations and maintenance costs of the electricity network and generation assets, other than staff and fuel, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes spare parts, consumables, contracted maintenance, repairs and servicing directly attributable to generating and delivering electricity; excludes staff costs (captured separately), fuel and oil, and general corporate overheads. Capitalised asset renewals are excluded, as they are recognised through depreciation rather than as an operating expense.
synonyms: ["operations and maintenance cost","direct o&m","maintenance expense","network o&m cost"]
alternative_names: {"Direct O&M - Electricity":"Electricity O&M","Electricity Operations & Maintenance":"Electricity O&M","Direct Costs: Electricity O&M":"Electricity O&M"}

name: Electricity Purchases
definition: Cost of electricity bought from third-party generators or interconnected providers for resale to customers, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes payments under power purchase agreements, independent power producer settlements and grid-import charges directly attributable to the electricity supplied; excludes the utility's own generation fuel, staff and O&M. Enter the purchased-power cost gross, before any netting of on-sold or wheeling revenue.
synonyms: ["purchased power cost","power purchase cost","electricity purchases","bulk supply cost"]
alternative_names: {"Purchased Power":"Electricity Purchases","Power Purchase Costs":"Electricity Purchases","Direct Costs: Electricity Purchases":"Electricity Purchases"}

name: Electricity Staff
definition: Salaries, wages and related employment costs of staff directly engaged in electricity generation, transmission and distribution, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes remuneration, overtime, allowances, superannuation and other on-costs for operational and technical personnel attributable to the electricity function; excludes corporate, administrative and support-staff costs, which belong in apportioned or other-staff lines. Where staff split time across functions, only the electricity-attributable share is captured here.
synonyms: ["direct labour cost","electricity staff costs","operational staff cost","direct employee costs"]
alternative_names: {"Electricity Staff Costs":"Electricity Staff","Direct Labour - Electricity":"Electricity Staff","Direct Costs: Electricity Staff":"Electricity Staff"}

name: Other O&M
definition: The share of general operations and maintenance and administrative overhead, other than staff and fuel, apportioned to the electricity function, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes office costs, insurance, IT, professional fees, vehicles and other corporate overheads not directly attributable to the network; excludes direct electricity O&M, fuel and staff costs. Apportion on the utility's standard basis and apply it consistently to keep the split between direct and apportioned costs comparable over time.
synonyms: ["overhead cost","apportioned overhead","administrative expense","general o&m"]
alternative_names: {"Apportioned Overhead":"Other O&M","Apportioned Cost: Other O&M":"Other O&M"}

name: Other Staff
definition: The share of non-direct staff costs (administrative, corporate, finance, commercial and support personnel) apportioned to the electricity function, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes salaries, allowances and employment on-costs for staff not directly engaged in generation or network operations; excludes direct electricity staff, which are reported separately. The apportionment basis (for example headcount, cost or revenue share) should follow the utility's standard costing method and be applied consistently year to year.
synonyms: ["overhead staff cost","administrative staff cost","apportioned labour","support staff cost"]
alternative_names: {"Other Staff Costs":"Other Staff","Apportioned Overhead Staff":"Other Staff","Apportioned Cost: Other Staff":"Other Staff"}

name: Amortization Expenses
definition: The systematic charge recognising the consumption of intangible assets over the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Covers software, licences, capitalised development costs, goodwill where amortised, and similar intangibles written down over their useful lives; it is a non-cash expense and excludes depreciation of tangible assets, which is reported separately. Amortisation applies to intangibles whereas depreciation applies to physical assets; do not combine the two.
synonyms: ["amortisation","amortisation charge","intangible amortisation"]
alternative_names: {"Amortisation":"Amortization Expenses","Amortisation Expense":"Amortization Expenses"}

name: Bad Debt Expense
definition: The charge recognised in the period for trade receivables judged unlikely to be collected, entered in the utility's local currency. Comprises the movement in the provision (allowance) for doubtful debts plus any receivables written off directly during the period; it is a non-cash expense reflecting expected credit losses on customer accounts. Enter the expense for the period only, not the cumulative provision balance, which sits within the receivables and balance-sheet figures.
synonyms: ["doubtful debts expense","provision for bad debts","impairment of receivables","credit loss expense"]
alternative_names: {"Doubtful Debts":"Bad Debt Expense","Provision for Bad Debts":"Bad Debt Expense","Impairment of Receivables":"Bad Debt Expense"}

name: Cost of Sales
definition: The direct cost of generating and delivering electricity sold during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes fuel and lubricating oil, purchased power, direct generation and network operations and maintenance, and direct operating staff costs; excludes administrative and corporate overheads, which belong in Other Operating Expenses, and excludes depreciation, interest and tax. This is the electricity equivalent of cost of goods sold and should reconcile with the sum of the direct and apportioned cost lines.
synonyms: ["cost of goods sold","cost of electricity sold","direct costs","cogs"]
alternative_names: {"Cost of Goods Sold":"Cost of Sales","COGS":"Cost of Sales","Cost of Electricity Sold":"Cost of Sales"}

name: Depreciation Expense
definition: The systematic charge recognising the consumption of tangible fixed assets over the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Covers generation plant, network infrastructure, buildings, vehicles and equipment written down over their useful lives; it is a non-cash expense and excludes amortisation of intangible assets, which is reported separately. Depreciation applies to physical assets whereas amortisation applies to intangibles; keep the two distinct.
synonyms: ["depreciation","depreciation charge","asset depreciation"]
alternative_names: {"Depreciation":"Depreciation Expense","Depreciation Charge":"Depreciation Expense"}

name: Financing Income
definition: Income earned from financial assets and cash management during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes interest on bank deposits and short-term investments, dividends received and other returns on financial instruments; excludes operating revenue and foreign-exchange gains, which are reported separately. Report financing income gross, without offsetting it against interest or other financing costs.
synonyms: ["interest income","investment income","finance income"]
alternative_names: {"Interest Income":"Financing Income","Investment Income":"Financing Income"}

name: Foreign Exchange Gains
definition: Gains arising from movements in foreign-currency exchange rates during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes realised gains on settling foreign-currency transactions and unrealised gains on retranslating foreign-currency assets and liabilities (such as fuel payables or foreign-denominated loans) at period end; it is reported as income. Enter foreign-exchange gains and losses on their separate lines rather than as a single net figure.
synonyms: ["fx gains","forex gains","exchange gains","foreign currency gains"]
alternative_names: {"FX Gains":"Foreign Exchange Gains","Forex Gains":"Foreign Exchange Gains"}

name: Foreign Exchange Losses
definition: Losses arising from movements in foreign-currency exchange rates during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes realised losses on settling foreign-currency transactions and unrealised losses on retranslating foreign-currency assets and liabilities (such as fuel payables or foreign-denominated loans) at period end; it is reported as a cost. Enter foreign-exchange gains and losses separately rather than netting them into one figure.
synonyms: ["fx losses","forex losses","exchange losses","foreign currency losses"]
alternative_names: {"FX Losses":"Foreign Exchange Losses","Forex Losses":"Foreign Exchange Losses"}

name: Government Subsidies
definition: Financial support received from government to support electricity operations or tariffs during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes operating subsidies, tariff or fuel subsidies, community-service-obligation payments and similar transfers received or receivable; it is distinct from capital grants for asset funding. Subsidies may be booked as income or netted against costs in different utilities' accounts, so enter the amount as received income here to keep treatment consistent across the benchmark.
synonyms: ["government subsidy","operating subsidy","government grant","community service obligation payment"]
alternative_names: {"Government Grant":"Government Subsidies","Operating Subsidy":"Government Subsidies","CSO Payment":"Government Subsidies"}

name: Income Tax
definition: The income tax expense attributable to the period's profit, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes current tax payable on taxable profit and, where applicable, the deferred-tax charge or credit; excludes indirect taxes such as VAT, GST, import duty and fuel excise, which are captured elsewhere. State-owned utilities that are tax-exempt or pay a dividend in lieu of tax should enter zero here and record any such payment under the appropriate line.
synonyms: ["income tax expense","corporate tax","tax expense","company tax"]
alternative_names: {"Income Tax Expense":"Income Tax","Corporate Tax":"Income Tax","Tax Expense":"Income Tax"}

name: Interest Expense
definition: The cost of borrowing recognised during the period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes interest on loans, bonds, overdrafts, leases and other debt instruments, together with the finance-charge element of borrowings; excludes principal repayments, which are balance-sheet movements, and other financing costs such as arrangement or guarantee fees where these are captured separately. Report interest gross, before offsetting any financing or interest income.
synonyms: ["interest cost","finance cost","borrowing cost","interest on debt"]
alternative_names: {"Finance Costs":"Interest Expense","Interest on Borrowings":"Interest Expense"}

name: Other Extraordinary Costs
definition: One-off or non-recurring costs falling outside the normal course of business, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes items such as disaster and storm damage, asset write-offs, restructuring and redundancy costs, litigation settlements and losses from unusual events not expected to recur; excludes routine operating expenses, cost of sales, interest and tax. Isolating extraordinary items keeps recurring operating results comparable across utilities and years.
synonyms: ["extraordinary costs","exceptional costs","non-recurring costs","one-off costs"]
alternative_names: {"Extraordinary Costs":"Other Extraordinary Costs","Exceptional Costs":"Other Extraordinary Costs"}

name: Other Extraordinary Income
definition: One-off or non-recurring income falling outside the normal course of business, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes items such as insurance settlements, one-time grants, reversals of prior provisions and gains from unusual events not expected to recur; excludes routine operating revenue, other income and government subsidies, which are reported separately. Isolating extraordinary items keeps recurring operating results comparable across utilities and years.
synonyms: ["extraordinary income","exceptional income","non-recurring income","one-off income"]
alternative_names: {"Extraordinary Income":"Other Extraordinary Income","Exceptional Income":"Other Extraordinary Income"}

name: Other Financing Costs
definition: Financing-related charges other than interest expense, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes loan arrangement and commitment fees, guarantee fees, bank charges on borrowings, and the unwinding of discounts on provisions; excludes interest expense itself and principal repayments. Report these costs separately from interest so that the interest burden and ancillary financing costs can each be analysed.
synonyms: ["finance charges","bank charges","loan fees","other finance costs"]
alternative_names: {"Other Finance Costs":"Other Financing Costs","Financing Charges":"Other Financing Costs"}

name: Other Income
definition: Income earned outside the core electricity supply business, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes rental income, gains on asset disposals, sundry recoveries, contract work for third parties and other miscellaneous operating income not classified as electricity revenue; excludes electricity sales, financing income, foreign-exchange gains and government subsidies, which have dedicated lines. Enter as gross income received, before netting against any related costs.
synonyms: ["miscellaneous income","sundry income","non-operating income","other operating income"]
alternative_names: {"Sundry Income":"Other Income","Miscellaneous Income":"Other Income"}

name: Other Operating Expenses
definition: Administrative, corporate and overhead operating expenses that are not part of the direct cost of sales, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes head-office costs, administrative salaries, insurance, professional fees, IT, office and general running costs; excludes cost of sales, bad debt expense, depreciation, amortisation, interest and income tax, each of which is reported separately. Do not include capital expenditure, which is recognised through depreciation rather than as an operating expense.
synonyms: ["administrative expenses","overhead expenses","operating expenses","opex"]
alternative_names: {"Administrative Expenses":"Other Operating Expenses","Overheads":"Other Operating Expenses","OPEX":"Other Operating Expenses"}

name: Profit
definition: The utility's net profit for the period, computed by PRISM (not entered) from the income statement: revenue plus other income, financing income, foreign-exchange gains and extraordinary income, less cost of sales, other operating expenses, depreciation, amortisation, interest, foreign-exchange losses, other financing costs, income tax and extraordinary costs. This is an after-tax net result (not operating profit); a negative value is a loss. Entered components are in local currency.
synonyms: ["net profit","net income","profit or loss","surplus or deficit","bottom line"]
alternative_names: {"Net Profit":"Profit","Net Income":"Profit","Profit/(Loss)":"Profit"}
formula: revenue_currency - cost_of_sales_currency - other_operating_expenses_currency + other_income_currency - depreciation_expense_currency - amortization_expenses_currency - interest_expense_currency + foreign_exchange_gains_currency - foreign_exchange_losses_currency + financing_income_currency - other_financing_costs_currency - income_tax_currency + other_extraordinary_income_currency - other_extraordinary_costs_currency

name: Revenue
definition: Operating revenue earned by the utility from its electricity business over the reporting period, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes electricity sales to all customer classes, connection and reconnection fees, and other charges arising directly from supplying electricity; excludes non-operating income, government subsidies, financing income and foreign-exchange gains, which are reported on their own lines. Revenue is recognised on an accruals basis (energy billed or delivered), not on cash received.
synonyms: ["operating revenue","electricity sales revenue","turnover","sales revenue"]
alternative_names: {"Operating Revenue":"Revenue","Electricity Sales":"Revenue","Turnover":"Revenue"}

name: Total Assets
definition: The total value of all assets controlled by the utility at the reporting date, entered in the utility's local currency. It is the sum of current assets and non-current assets, the latter including property, plant and equipment (generation, network and buildings), intangibles and long-term investments, stated net of accumulated depreciation and amortisation. This balance-sheet total should equal total equity plus total liabilities.
synonyms: ["total assets","balance sheet total"]
alternative_names: {"Balance Sheet Total":"Total Assets"}

name: Total Costs
definition: The utility's total operating cost for the period, computed by PRISM (not entered) as the sum of the eight cost-breakdown lines: direct electricity staff, O&M and power-purchase costs, plus apportioned fuel & oil, other staff, other O&M, and duty/tax lines. It is an operating-cost total (fuel, O&M, labour, purchases, duties) and excludes depreciation, interest, tax and extraordinary items, which sit in the income statement. Entered in local currency; used as the cost basis for cost-per-kWh and operating-efficiency KPIs.
synonyms: ["total expenses","total expenditure","total operating and non-operating costs"]
alternative_names: {"Total Expenses":"Total Costs","Total Expenditure":"Total Costs"}

name: Total Current Assets
definition: The total of assets expected to be realised, sold or consumed within twelve months of the reporting date, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes cash and cash equivalents, trade and other receivables, inventories (including fuel and spares stock) and short-term investments and prepayments; excludes property, plant, equipment and other non-current assets. This is a balance-sheet total measured at the period-end date, not a flow over the period.
synonyms: ["current assets","short-term assets"]
alternative_names: {"Current Assets":"Total Current Assets"}

name: Total Current Liabilities
definition: The total of obligations due to be settled within twelve months of the reporting date, entered in the utility's local currency. Includes trade and other payables, accrued expenses, the current portion of borrowings and leases, short-term provisions, and customer deposits repayable within the year; excludes long-term debt and other non-current liabilities. This is a balance-sheet total measured at period end, used with current assets to assess short-term liquidity.
synonyms: ["current liabilities","short-term liabilities"]
alternative_names: {"Current Liabilities":"Total Current Liabilities"}

name: Total Equity
definition: The residual interest in the utility's assets after deducting all liabilities, entered in the utility's local currency at the reporting date. Includes share or contributed capital, retained earnings or accumulated losses, government capital contributions and reserves such as revaluation and other reserves. Equity equals total assets minus total liabilities; a negative figure indicates accumulated losses exceed contributed capital.
synonyms: ["shareholders equity","net assets","owners equity","capital and reserves"]
alternative_names: {"Shareholders' Equity":"Total Equity","Net Assets":"Total Equity","Capital and Reserves":"Total Equity"}

name: Total Liabilities
definition: The total of all obligations owed by the utility at the reporting date, entered in the utility's local currency. It is the sum of current liabilities and non-current liabilities, the latter including long-term borrowings, lease liabilities, deferred tax and long-term provisions and deferred income; it excludes equity. This balance-sheet total equals total assets minus total equity.
synonyms: ["total liabilities","total debt and obligations"]
alternative_names: {"Total Obligations":"Total Liabilities"}

name: Trade Receivables
definition: The amount owed to the utility by customers for electricity billed but not yet paid at the reporting date, entered in the utility's local currency. This is a balance-sheet figure normally reported net of the provision for doubtful debts; it includes amounts due from all customer classes for energy and related charges and excludes non-trade receivables such as loans, staff advances and prepayments. State whether the figure is gross or net of provision consistently, as this affects receivable-days and collection ratios computed downstream.
synonyms: ["accounts receivable","trade debtors","receivables","debtors"]
alternative_names: {"Accounts Receivable":"Trade Receivables","Trade Debtors":"Trade Receivables","Debtors":"Trade Receivables"}

name: USD Exchange Rate
definition: The exchange rate between the utility's local currency and the US dollar for the reporting period, expressed as the number of local currency units per 1 USD. For example, if 1 USD buys 2.20 local units, enter 2.20. This rate lets PRISM convert locally reported currency figures into a common USD basis for cross-utility comparison; use a consistent period-average or period-end convention as specified by the benchmark.
synonyms: ["exchange rate","usd rate","fx rate","local currency per usd"]
alternative_names: {"Exchange Rate (USD)":"USD Exchange Rate","FX Rate":"USD Exchange Rate","USD Rate":"USD Exchange Rate"}

name: Tariff Block Limit
definition: The cumulative consumption threshold, in kWh measured FROM ZERO, at which one tariff rate ends and the next begins. For a tariff with N rates there are N-1 block limits: Block Limit 1 is the cumulative kWh up to which Rate 1 applies, Block Limit 2 is where Rate 2 gives way to Rate 3, and so on; the final rate runs indefinitely with no upper limit. Enter the CUMULATIVE figure from zero (the upper bound of the block) — never the width of the block, and never an amount relative to the previous block's limit. Block limits must increase strictly (Limit 1 < Limit 2 < ...). At entry the lower bound is shown auto-filled (0 for the first block, the previous limit thereafter) so only the cumulative upper bound is keyed.
synonyms: ["block threshold","consumption block limit","tariff band limit","step limit"]
alternative_names: {"Block Limit":"Tariff Block Limit","Block Threshold":"Tariff Block Limit","Consumption Band Limit":"Tariff Block Limit"}

name: Tariff Fixed Monthly Charge
definition: The fixed monthly service/standing charge levied on a customer regardless of consumption, entered in the utility's local currency and EXCLUDING VAT/GST (tax captured separately). Enter the TAX-EXCLUSIVE amount; the tax-inclusive figure customers pay is derived as charge x (1 + tax rate) and shown at entry for verification.
synonyms: ["fixed charge","standing charge","service charge","monthly fixed fee"]
alternative_names: {"Fixed Charge":"Tariff Fixed Monthly Charge","Standing Charge":"Tariff Fixed Monthly Charge","Service Charge":"Tariff Fixed Monthly Charge"}

name: Tariff Rate per kwh within the Block
definition: The per-kWh charge applying to consumption within a given tariff block, entered in the utility's local currency and EXCLUDING VAT/GST (tax is captured separately as the Tariff VAT or GST Rate measure). Rate 1 applies from zero up to Block Limit 1, Rate 2 from Block Limit 1 to Block Limit 2, and the final rate indefinitely. Enter the TAX-EXCLUSIVE rate; the customer-facing tax-inclusive figure is derived as rate x (1 + tax rate) and shown at entry for verification against the published rate.
synonyms: ["energy charge","unit rate","volumetric rate","price per kwh","tariff rate"]
alternative_names: {"Rate per kWh":"Tariff Rate per kwh within the Block","Energy Charge":"Tariff Rate per kwh within the Block","Unit Rate":"Tariff Rate per kwh within the Block"}

name: Tariff VAT or GST Rate
definition: The rate of value-added tax or goods-and-services tax applied to electricity charges under the utility's tariff schedule, expressed as a percentage. It is the indirect-tax rate added to the customer's bill on top of energy and fixed charges; the customer class, block or payment mode to which it applies is handled by dimensions, so define it generically as the applicable VAT or GST rate. Enter the statutory rate as a proportion (for example 0.15 for 15 per cent), not the tax amount collected.
synonyms: ["vat rate","gst rate","sales tax rate","consumption tax rate"]
alternative_names: {"VAT Rate":"Tariff VAT or GST Rate","GST Rate":"Tariff VAT or GST Rate"}

name: Are line/sector Ministers or Public Servants appointed to the Board?
definition: Records whether any serving line or sector Minister, or a public servant from a government ministry or department, currently holds a seat on the utility's governing board. It captures the degree of direct political and executive-government presence in board-level decision-making. Answer Yes only if at least one such person is a sitting board member during the reporting year, whether as a full voting director or an ex-officio member; a purely advisory attendee who is not appointed to the board does not count. For a Pacific state-owned utility this matters because ministerial or civil-servant board seats can blur the line between shareholder oversight and day-to-day management, weakening the depoliticised, arm's-length governance that supports commercial performance.
synonyms: ["ministerial board appointment","public servant directors","government officials on board","political board representation"]
alternative_names: {"Are government officials appointed to the Board?":"Are line/sector Ministers or Public Servants appointed to the Board?","Ministers or civil servants on the Board":"Are line/sector Ministers or Public Servants appointed to the Board?"}

name: Are Ministers appointed to the Board?
definition: Records whether one or more serving government Ministers hold a seat on the utility's governing board. It is a narrower measure than the combined Minister-or-public-servant question, isolating direct ministerial presence at board level. Answer Yes only if a sitting Minister is a formally appointed board member during the reporting year, as either a voting director or an ex-officio member. Ministerial board seats are a governance concern for a Pacific state-owned utility because they concentrate political authority in the boardroom and can compromise the board's independence from the executive branch.
synonyms: ["ministers on the board","ministerial directorship","cabinet member on board"]
alternative_names: {"Is a Minister a Board member?":"Are Ministers appointed to the Board?","Ministerial seat on the Board":"Are Ministers appointed to the Board?"}

name: Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan?
definition: Records whether the utility's annual report reports actual performance against the objectives and targets set out in its strategic plan. It captures the accountability link between planning and public reporting. Answer Yes only if the annual report for the reporting year explicitly compares results with strategic-plan goals or targets, rather than merely describing the year's activities; a report with no reference back to the plan counts as No. This disclosure matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because it closes the loop between strategy and results, letting the shareholder and public judge whether commitments were met.
synonyms: ["performance against plan disclosure","strategic plan reporting","results versus plan","plan performance disclosure"]
alternative_names: {"Does the Annual Report report against the Strategic Plan?":"Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan?","Reporting against strategic targets":"Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan?"}

name: Does the CEO's Performance Contract include Annual Reviews?
definition: Records whether the CEO's performance contract provides for a formal review of performance at least once a year. It captures the presence of a recurring appraisal mechanism within the contract, not merely the contract's existence. Answer Yes only if the current contract specifies an annual (or more frequent) performance review, and such a review mechanism is operative during the reporting year; a contract with objectives but no scheduled review process does not count. Annual reviews matter for a Pacific state-owned utility because they give the board a regular, structured point at which to assess executive delivery and reinforce accountability.
synonyms: ["annual CEO appraisal","yearly performance review","annual performance assessment","CEO annual evaluation"]
alternative_names: {"Does the CEO contract require annual reviews?":"Does the CEO's Performance Contract include Annual Reviews?","Annual CEO performance review":"Does the CEO's Performance Contract include Annual Reviews?"}

name: Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts?
definition: Records whether the utility's adopted strategic plan contains forward-looking forecasts covering a horizon of at least three years. It captures the plan's medium-term planning depth rather than its existence alone. Answer Yes only if the current plan sets out projections, such as financial, demand, capital or operational forecasts, spanning three or more future years; a plan limited to a single year or the year ahead only does not count. A multi-year forecasting horizon matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because capital-intensive assets and tariff decisions require planning well beyond the current budget cycle.
synonyms: ["multi-year forecasts","three-year forecast horizon","medium-term projections","forward forecasts in plan"]
alternative_names: {"Does the plan cover three or more years?":"Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts?","Multi-year forecasting in Strategic Plan":"Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts?"}

name: Has a Strategic Plan been adopted?
definition: Records whether the utility has a formally adopted strategic plan setting out its medium-term objectives, priorities and direction. It captures the existence of a board-approved plan, separate from the plan's content or execution. Answer Yes only if a strategic plan has been formally approved or endorsed by the board and is current for the reporting year; a draft still in preparation or a lapsed plan does not count. A current strategic plan matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because it provides a shared framework for accountability, investment prioritisation and monitoring by the board and shareholder.
synonyms: ["corporate plan","business plan adopted","strategic plan approved","medium-term plan"]
alternative_names: {"Is a Strategic Plan adopted?":"Has a Strategic Plan been adopted?","Corporate Plan in place":"Has a Strategic Plan been adopted?"}

name: Is a Code of Conduct implemented?
definition: Records whether the utility's adopted Code of Conduct is actively applied in practice rather than existing only on paper. It distinguishes real operation of the Code, such as staff acknowledgement, breach reporting and enforcement, from mere adoption. Answer Yes only if the Code is demonstrably in use during the reporting year, evidenced by measures such as induction and training, signed acknowledgements, a functioning reporting or disciplinary process, or documented enforcement actions. For a Pacific state-owned utility, an implemented Code turns stated ethical standards into an accountability mechanism, reinforcing integrity and public trust.
synonyms: ["code of conduct enforced","ethics policy applied","code in operation","code compliance active"]
alternative_names: {"Is the Code of Conduct enforced?":"Is a Code of Conduct implemented?","Code of Ethics operationalised":"Is a Code of Conduct implemented?"}

name: Is a Code of Conduct in place?
definition: Records whether the utility has a formally adopted Code of Conduct setting out the ethical standards and expected behaviour of directors, management and staff. This captures the existence of the document as an approved governance instrument, distinct from whether it is actively applied. Answer Yes only if a written Code has been formally adopted or approved by the board and is current for the reporting year; a draft under consideration or an expired policy does not count. A Code of Conduct is a foundational integrity control for a Pacific state-owned utility, signalling a commitment to ethical conduct, conflict-of-interest management and anti-corruption norms.
synonyms: ["code of ethics","ethics policy","conduct policy","business conduct standards"]
alternative_names: {"Does a Code of Conduct exist?":"Is a Code of Conduct in place?","Code of Ethics adopted":"Is a Code of Conduct in place?"}

name: Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?
definition: Records whether the utility's commercial mandate is actively pursued in practice rather than existing only as a stated objective. It distinguishes real application, such as cost-reflective decision-making and financial performance targets, from mere adoption of the mandate. Answer Yes only if the mandate is demonstrably driving operations during the reporting year, evidenced by measures such as commercially oriented budgets, tariff or cost-recovery efforts, and management accountability for financial results. For a Pacific state-owned utility, an implemented commercial mandate is what translates a policy of financial sustainability into actual pricing, cost control and investment behaviour.
synonyms: ["commercial mandate applied","commercial objectives pursued","cost-recovery operation","commercial mandate enforced"]
alternative_names: {"Is the Commercial Mandate being applied?":"Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?","Commercial mandate operationalised":"Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?"}

name: Is a Commercial Mandate in place?
definition: Records whether the utility operates under a formally established commercial mandate, meaning an approved directive or statutory objective requiring it to run on a commercial, financially sustainable basis. This captures the existence of the mandate as an authorised instrument, separate from whether it is being applied. Answer Yes only if a commercial mandate has been formally set out and approved, for example in the utility's enabling legislation, statement of corporate intent, shareholder directive or board-endorsed policy, and is current for the reporting year. A clear commercial mandate matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because it establishes the expectation of cost recovery and financial discipline rather than open-ended reliance on subsidy.
synonyms: ["commercial objective","commercial orientation directive","statement of corporate intent","commercial operating mandate"]
alternative_names: {"Does a Commercial Mandate exist?":"Is a Commercial Mandate in place?","Commercial mandate established":"Is a Commercial Mandate in place?"}

name: Is the Annual Report audited?
definition: Records whether the utility's annual report, and in particular its financial statements, is subject to an independent external audit. It captures the presence of independent assurance over reported results. Answer Yes only if the annual report for the reporting year has been audited by an independent external auditor and carries an audit opinion; internal review alone, or financial statements not yet audited, counts as No. Independent audit matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because it provides credible, third-party assurance to the shareholder, lenders and public that the reported financial position is reliable.
synonyms: ["audited annual report","external audit","independent audit","audited financial statements"]
alternative_names: {"Are the financial statements audited?":"Is the Annual Report audited?","External audit of Annual Report":"Is the Annual Report audited?"}

name: Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the Reporting Year?
definition: Records whether the utility finalises its annual report within four months of the close of its reporting year. It captures the timeliness of annual financial and performance reporting. Answer Yes only if the annual report for the reporting year was completed, meaning finalised and issued, no later than four months after the reporting year-end; completion beyond that window, or a report not yet completed, counts as No. Timely annual reporting matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because prompt disclosure to the shareholder, regulator and public underpins transparency and allows performance issues to be acted on while still current.
synonyms: ["timely annual report","annual report within four months","reporting timeliness","prompt annual reporting"]
alternative_names: {"Is the Annual Report issued within four months?":"Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the Reporting Year?","Annual Report completed on time":"Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the Reporting Year?"}

name: Is the CEO on a Performance Contract?
definition: Records whether the utility's Chief Executive Officer is engaged under a performance contract that ties their tenure or remuneration to defined objectives and results. It captures the existence of a formal performance-based agreement, separate from any review mechanism within it. Answer Yes only if a current, signed performance contract with measurable objectives is in force for the CEO during the reporting year; an ordinary employment contract with no performance targets does not count. A CEO performance contract matters for a Pacific state-owned utility because it is a primary lever for holding executive leadership accountable to the board and shareholder for delivery.
synonyms: ["CEO performance agreement","executive performance contract","CEO KPI contract","performance-based CEO contract"]
alternative_names: {"Does the CEO have a performance contract?":"Is the CEO on a Performance Contract?","CEO on performance agreement":"Is the CEO on a Performance Contract?"}

name: Is the Strategic Plan implemented?
definition: Records whether the utility's adopted strategic plan is actively being executed rather than sitting unused after approval. It distinguishes real implementation, such as translating the plan into budgets, projects and monitored targets, from mere adoption. Answer Yes only if the plan is demonstrably guiding activity during the reporting year, evidenced by measures such as aligned annual budgets, tracked initiatives, progress reporting to the board, or delivery against plan milestones. For a Pacific state-owned utility, an implemented strategic plan is what converts stated priorities into actual resource allocation and measurable performance.
synonyms: ["strategic plan executed","plan in operation","strategy being delivered","plan implementation active"]
alternative_names: {"Is the Strategic Plan being executed?":"Is the Strategic Plan implemented?","Strategy operationalised":"Is the Strategic Plan implemented?"}

name: FTE Employees
definition: The size of the utility's workforce expressed in full-time equivalents (FTE), where each unit represents one full-time working schedule. Permanent full-time and part-time staff on the payroll are converted to FTE on the basis of hours worked, so that two half-time employees count as one FTE; contractors and consultants are excluded. Unlike a plain headcount, FTE reflects the true labour capacity of the utility and is the appropriate denominator for productivity ratios such as customers or connections per employee.
synonyms: ["full-time equivalent employees","FTE headcount","full-time equivalents","equivalent full-time staff","FTE workforce"]
alternative_names: {"Full-Time Equivalent Employees":"FTE Employees","FTE Headcount":"FTE Employees","Full-Time Equivalents":"FTE Employees"}

name: Employees
definition: The headcount of people directly employed by the utility, expressed as a number of employees. It counts permanent full-time and part-time staff on the payroll, and excludes contractors, consultants and other outsourced labour. The headcount is sliced by division and by gender through separate dimensions, which supports PPA gender-representation reporting; note that headcount treats a part-time person the same as a full-time one, so it will read higher than the equivalent full-time-equivalent (FTE) figure.
synonyms: ["headcount","staff count","number of employees","workforce","staff numbers","personnel"]
alternative_names: {"Headcount":"Employees","Staff Count":"Employees","Number of Employees":"Employees"}

name: Gender
definition: An option-typed attribute that records the gender of an employee or role, selected from the platform's standard Gender list rather than entered as a number. It classifies workforce records so that headcount and other HR measures can be sliced by gender through a dimension. Consistent use of the same gender categories across all utilities is what makes the resulting gender-representation reporting to the PPA comparable.
synonyms: ["sex","gender category","gender classification","gender dimension"]
alternative_names: {"Sex":"Gender","Gender Category":"Gender","Gender Classification":"Gender"}

name: Hours lost to Work Related Injuries
definition: The total number of working hours lost as a result of work-related injuries during the period, expressed in hours. It captures time an employee would otherwise have worked but could not because of a lost-time injury sustained on the job, following standard occupational health and safety (OHS) conventions; it excludes absence unrelated to workplace injury such as ordinary sick leave or annual leave. The figure feeds injury-severity and lost-time measures, so consistent counting of the first day off and of partial days is important for comparability across utilities.
synonyms: ["lost time hours","injury hours lost","lost workdays in hours","days lost to injury","hours lost to injury"]
alternative_names: {"Lost Time Hours":"Hours lost to Work Related Injuries","Injury Hours Lost":"Hours lost to Work Related Injuries","Hours Lost to Injury":"Hours lost to Work Related Injuries"}

name: Number of Work Related Injuries
definition: The count of work-related injuries recorded during the period, expressed as a number of incidents. Following standard occupational health and safety (OHS) conventions it covers injuries arising out of the course of employment, typically those serious enough to be reported or to result in lost time, and excludes non-work-related or off-duty injuries. Because utilities differ in size, this raw count is usually read alongside hours worked as a frequency rate per million hours; small workforces produce small counts, so year-on-year swings can look large in relative terms.
synonyms: ["work related injuries","injury count","number of injuries","reportable injuries","workplace injuries","lost time injuries"]
alternative_names: {"Work Related Injuries":"Number of Work Related Injuries","Injury Count":"Number of Work Related Injuries","Workplace Injuries":"Number of Work Related Injuries"}

name: Hours Paid
definition: The total number of hours the utility paid its staff for over the period, expressed in hours. It includes hours actually worked as well as paid time not worked, such as annual leave, sick leave and public holidays, but excludes unpaid absence. Set against actual and standard hours, it underpins staff-utilisation measures; the gap between hours paid and hours worked is a useful signal of leave and absence loading, so the two should be recorded on a consistent basis.
synonyms: ["paid hours","hours paid for","payroll hours","compensated hours","total paid time"]
alternative_names: {"Paid Hours":"Hours Paid","Payroll Hours":"Hours Paid","Compensated Hours":"Hours Paid"}

name: Hours Worked Actual
definition: The actual number of hours worked by the utility's staff over the period, expressed in hours. It records time genuinely spent working, including overtime and excluding hours paid but not worked such as leave or public holidays. Compared against standard and paid hours it drives staff-utilisation and productivity measures, so overtime and time-recording practices should be captured consistently to keep the ratios meaningful.
synonyms: ["actual hours","hours worked","productive hours","time worked","actual working hours"]
alternative_names: {"Actual Hours":"Hours Worked Actual","Hours Worked":"Hours Worked Actual","Productive Hours":"Hours Worked Actual"}

name: Hours Worked Standard
definition: The standard, or rostered, number of working hours for the utility's staff over the period, expressed in hours. It represents the contracted or scheduled hours that employees would work under normal conditions, before any overtime, absence or leave is taken into account. Used together with actual and paid hours, it forms the baseline for staff-utilisation measures; because it is a scheduled figure rather than a recorded one, it should reflect the standard working week applied consistently across the workforce.
synonyms: ["standard hours","rostered hours","scheduled hours","contracted hours","normal working hours"]
alternative_names: {"Standard Hours":"Hours Worked Standard","Rostered Hours":"Hours Worked Standard","Scheduled Hours":"Hours Worked Standard"}

name: Rated Capacity
definition: The nameplate (installed) real-power capacity of a generating unit, expressed in MW. It is the manufacturer-rated continuous output of the unit and is recorded per unit at equipment level, sliced by energy source and provider via the dimension columns rather than defined per fuel. PRISM aggregates unit ratings up to station, service-area and utility totals; be clear whether gross nameplate or net (derated) capacity is being entered, and keep MW capacity distinct from MWh energy.
synonyms: ["installed capacity","nameplate capacity","rated output","generating capacity","plant capacity"]
alternative_names: {"Installed Capacity (MW)":"Rated Capacity","Nameplate Capacity":"Rated Capacity","Rated Output":"Rated Capacity"}

name: Customers Served
definition: The number of connected customer accounts (metered service points) supplied with electricity during the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. It counts active connections or billing accounts, not the number of people, and is sliced by customer type, service area and provider via the dimension columns rather than by name. This count is the denominator for per-customer benchmarks and for the SAIDI/SAIFI reliability indices, so count connections consistently and do not confuse it with population served.
synonyms: ["connections","customer connections","connected customers","customer accounts","number of customers","service points"]
alternative_names: {"No. of Customers":"Customers Served","Total Connections":"Customers Served","Customer Accounts":"Customers Served"}

name: Equipment Planned Downtime Events
definition: Number of planned (scheduled) outage events for a generation or storage unit during the period, at equipment grain per unit. Sliced by resource type (Generator / Energy Storage) and the unit's provider/type/source via the registry. Equipment downtime only — network (T&D) downtime is a separate measure.
synonyms: ["scheduled outages","planned maintenance shutdowns","scheduled downtime count","planned outage events"]
alternative_names: {"Scheduled Outages":"Equipment Planned Downtime Events","Planned Maintenance Events":"Equipment Planned Downtime Events","Equipment Planned Downtime Count":"Equipment Planned Downtime Events"}

name: Equipment Planned Downtime Hours
definition: Total hours a generation or storage unit was out of service due to planned (scheduled) maintenance during the period, at equipment grain per unit. Sliced by resource type (Generator / Energy Storage) and the unit's provider/type/source. Equipment downtime only — network downtime is separate.
synonyms: ["scheduled outage hours","planned maintenance hours","planned unavailability hours"]
alternative_names: {"Scheduled Downtime Hours":"Equipment Planned Downtime Hours","Planned Outage Duration":"Equipment Planned Downtime Hours","Equipment Planned Downtime Duration":"Equipment Planned Downtime Hours"}

name: Equipment Unplanned Downtime Events
definition: Number of unplanned (forced) outage events — trips and component failures — for a generation or storage unit during the period, at equipment grain per unit. Sliced by resource type (Generator / Energy Storage) and the unit's provider/type/source. Equipment downtime only — network downtime is separate.
synonyms: ["forced outages","unscheduled outages","breakdown events","trips","forced downtime count"]
alternative_names: {"Forced Outages":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Events","Unscheduled Downtime Events":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Events","Equipment Unplanned Downtime Count":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Events"}

name: Equipment Unplanned Downtime Hours
definition: Total hours a generation or storage unit was out of service due to unplanned (forced) outages — trips and component failures — during the period, at equipment grain per unit. Sliced by resource type (Generator / Energy Storage) and the unit's provider/type/source. Equipment downtime only — network downtime is separate.
synonyms: ["forced outage hours","unscheduled downtime hours","forced unavailability hours","breakdown hours"]
alternative_names: {"Forced Outage Hours":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Hours","Unscheduled Downtime Hours":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Hours","Equipment Unplanned Downtime Duration":"Equipment Unplanned Downtime Hours"}

name: Network Planned Downtime Events
definition: The number of network outage events due to planned (scheduled) works during the period, attributed to the utility function (Transmission or Distribution). Network downtime only — generating-unit downtime is a separate measure.
synonyms: ["planned network outages","scheduled network outages","planned network maintenance events","scheduled network downtime count"]
alternative_names: {"Network Planned Downtime Count":"Network Planned Downtime Events"}

name: Network Planned Downtime Hours
definition: The total hours the transmission or distribution network was out of service due to planned (scheduled) works during the period, attributed to the utility function (Transmission or Distribution). Network downtime only — generating-unit downtime is a separate measure.
synonyms: ["planned network outage hours","scheduled network downtime duration","planned network maintenance hours","scheduled network outage hours"]
alternative_names: {"Network Planned Downtime Duration":"Network Planned Downtime Hours"}

name: Network Unplanned Downtime Events
definition: The number of network outage events due to unplanned (fault) outages during the period, attributed to the utility function (Transmission or Distribution). Network downtime only — generating-unit downtime is a separate measure.
synonyms: ["network faults","unplanned network outages","network fault events","forced network outages"]
alternative_names: {"Network Unplanned Downtime Count":"Network Unplanned Downtime Events"}

name: Network Unplanned Downtime Hours
definition: The total hours the transmission or distribution network was out of service due to unplanned (fault) outages during the period, attributed to the utility function (Transmission or Distribution). Network downtime only — generating-unit downtime is a separate measure.
synonyms: ["network fault hours","unplanned network outage duration","forced network outage hours","network interruption hours"]
alternative_names: {"Network Unplanned Downtime Duration":"Network Unplanned Downtime Hours"}

name: Electricity for Charging
definition: The electrical energy drawn to charge an energy storage system during the reporting period, expressed in kWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It is the energy consumed at the input to charge the battery, sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Because of charging and round-trip losses it exceeds the energy later discharged; keep it distinct from Energy Stored (energy absorbed) and Electricity Discharged (energy delivered out).
synonyms: ["charging energy","energy for charging","battery charge input","ESS charging energy"]
alternative_names: {"Charging Energy":"Electricity for Charging","Battery Charge Energy":"Electricity for Charging"}

name: Electricity Sold to Customers
definition: The metered electrical energy billed to customers during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. It is the revenue-generating energy that reaches customer meters, sliced by customer type, tariff and service area via the dimension columns. Together with energy sent out it defines system losses (energy sent out less energy sold), and with non-revenue energy it reconciles total delivered energy; confirm units are MWh, not kWh, when entering.
synonyms: ["units sold","energy sold","billed energy","electricity billed","revenue energy","energy sales"]
alternative_names: {"Units Sold (MWh)":"Electricity Sold to Customers","Energy Billed":"Electricity Sold to Customers","kWh Sold":"Electricity Sold to Customers"}

name: Non-Revenue Energy Consumed
definition: The electrical energy that entered the system but was not billed to customers during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. It comprises technical losses (in lines and transformers), commercial losses (theft, metering error, unbilled use) and any unmetered own consumption, sliced by loss type and service area via the dimension columns. It is the difference between energy delivered into the network and Electricity Sold to Customers, and underlies the non-revenue-energy / system-loss percentage; enter in MWh and avoid double-counting station auxiliaries.
synonyms: ["non-revenue energy","NRE","system losses","network losses","unbilled energy","energy losses"]
alternative_names: {"System Losses":"Non-Revenue Energy Consumed","Non-Revenue Energy":"Non-Revenue Energy Consumed","NRE (MWh)":"Non-Revenue Energy Consumed","Non-Revenue Electricity Consumed":"Non-Revenue Energy Consumed"}

name: Station Auxilliary Usage
definition: The electrical energy consumed by a power station's own auxiliary equipment during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded at the power-station level. It covers in-house loads such as pumps, fans, control systems and lighting that the station uses to operate, sliced by station and provider via the dimension columns. It is the difference between gross generation and net energy sent to grid, so include it when reconciling gross and net energy and avoid counting it as customer or network loss.
synonyms: ["auxiliary consumption","station auxiliaries","own use","in-house load","parasitic load","works power"]
alternative_names: {"Auxiliary Consumption":"Station Auxilliary Usage","Station Own Use":"Station Auxilliary Usage","Auxiliary Load":"Station Auxilliary Usage"}

name: Electricity Demand Average Load
definition: The average electrical demand placed on the system over the reporting period, expressed in MWh as the mean load, recorded at the service-area level. It represents the typical loading of the system rather than its extremes and is sliced by service area and provider via the dimension columns. Used with peak load to derive load factor; do not confuse average load with peak load or with total energy sent out.
synonyms: ["average demand","average load","mean system load","average system demand"]
alternative_names: {"Average Demand":"Electricity Demand Average Load","Mean Load":"Electricity Demand Average Load"}

name: Electricity Demand Peak Load
definition: The maximum electrical demand placed on the system during the reporting period, expressed in MWh as the peak load, recorded at the service-area level. It is the highest instantaneous or interval demand reached and is sliced by service area and provider via the dimension columns. Peak load sizes capacity requirements and, with average load, gives load factor; keep it distinct from average load and installed capacity.
synonyms: ["peak demand","maximum demand","system peak","peak load"]
alternative_names: {"Peak Demand":"Electricity Demand Peak Load","Maximum Demand":"Electricity Demand Peak Load","System Peak":"Electricity Demand Peak Load"}

name: Electricity Discharged
definition: The electrical energy delivered out of an energy storage system during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It is the energy the storage system returns to the network or load and is sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Because of round-trip losses it is less than the energy taken in to charge; keep it separate from Electricity for Charging (input) and Energy Stored.
synonyms: ["energy discharged","battery discharge","storage output energy","ESS energy out"]
alternative_names: {"Battery Discharge":"Electricity Discharged","Energy Discharged":"Electricity Discharged"}

name: Electricity Generated
definition: The gross electrical energy produced by a generating unit during the reporting period, measured at the unit's terminals before deduction of station auxiliary consumption, expressed in MWh. It is a single measure sliced by energy source and provider via the dimension columns, not a separate measure per fuel, and is recorded per unit at equipment level. Because this is gross generation, net energy sent out equals generation less station auxiliary usage; confirm gross-versus-net and MWh-versus-kWh conventions when entering.
synonyms: ["gross generation","units generated","energy generated","gross output","production","generation"]
alternative_names: {"Gross Generation":"Electricity Generated","Units Generated (MWh)":"Electricity Generated","Energy Produced":"Electricity Generated"}

name: Electricity Purchased from Other Providers
definition: The metered electrical energy bought from other generators or providers (for example independent power producers) during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded at the service-area level. It is energy the utility takes onto its system from third parties and is sliced by provider and energy source via the dimension columns. It adds to own generation in the supply balance; keep it distinct from own generation and from energy sold to customers.
synonyms: ["purchased power","energy purchased","IPP purchases","bought-in energy","power purchased"]
alternative_names: {"Purchased Power":"Electricity Purchased from Other Providers","Energy Purchased (MWh)":"Electricity Purchased from Other Providers","IPP Purchases":"Electricity Purchased from Other Providers"}

name: Electricity Sent to Grid
definition: The electrical energy delivered into the transmission/distribution network during the reporting period, expressed in MWh — i.e. energy sent out, measured where generation (own plant plus purchases) is injected into the grid, after deducting station auxiliary consumption. It equals Electricity Sold to Customers plus Non-Revenue Energy Consumed, and is the denominator for the system-loss / non-revenue-energy percentage. Enter in MWh (not kWh), measured at the sent-out / grid-injection point rather than gross generation, to avoid double-counting station auxiliaries.
synonyms: ["energy sent out","electricity sent out","net generation sent out","units sent out","energy delivered to grid","grid injection","energy into network"]
alternative_names: {"Energy Sent Out":"Electricity Sent to Grid","Electricity Sent Out":"Electricity Sent to Grid","Net Electricity Supplied":"Electricity Sent to Grid"}

name: Energy Stored
definition: The electrical energy taken into an energy storage system (for example a battery) during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It represents energy absorbed into storage and is sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Distinguish it from Electricity for Charging (energy drawn to charge) and Electricity Discharged (energy delivered back out); round-trip efficiency means stored and discharged energy differ.
synonyms: ["energy into storage","battery energy stored","storage charge energy","ESS energy in"]
alternative_names: {"Battery Energy Stored":"Energy Stored","Energy Into Storage":"Energy Stored"}

name: Fuel Oil
definition: The volume of fuel oil consumed by a generating unit during the reporting period, expressed in litres. It captures the liquid fuel burned to produce electricity (for example diesel or heavy fuel oil) and is recorded per generating unit at equipment level, sliced by fuel type and provider via the dimension columns. Used with generation to derive fuel efficiency and specific fuel consumption; keep it distinct from lubrication oil.
synonyms: ["diesel consumed","fuel consumed","fuel used","HFO consumption","generator fuel"]
alternative_names: {"Fuel Consumption":"Fuel Oil","Diesel Used (L)":"Fuel Oil"}

name: Lubrication Oil
definition: The volume of lubricating oil consumed by a generating unit during the reporting period, expressed in litres. It captures lube oil used and topped up in engine operation, recorded per generating unit at equipment level and sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. It is a maintenance and operating-cost input and should not be combined with fuel oil, which is the combustion fuel.
synonyms: ["lube oil consumed","lubricant used","engine oil consumption"]
alternative_names: {"Lube Oil":"Lubrication Oil","Lubricant Consumption":"Lubrication Oil"}

name: Total Planned Interruptions Customer Minutes
definition: The total customer-minutes lost to planned (scheduled and pre-notified) supply interruptions in the reporting period, being the sum over all affected customers of the duration each was without supply, expressed in customer-minutes.
